title: Purely inseparable invariants through a tensor compositum and two kernels
statement:
Let $K\subseteq L$ and $K\subseteq M$ be field extensions with $M/K$ finite, and suppose $T=L\otimes_K M$ is a field. Let a finite group $N$ act on $L$ and $M$ by field automorphisms preserving $K$, with the same action on $K$, and hence act diagonally on $T$. Let $Q\triangleleft N$ act trivially on $L$, and write $A=N/Q$ for its induced action on $L$. For a group $G$ acting on a field $E$, write $E^G=\{x\in E:g(x)=x\ \forall g\in G\}$. Suppose $M^Q/K$ is purely inseparable, and let $R\subseteq L^A$ be a subfield with $L^A/R$ purely inseparable. Then, under the canonical embeddings,
$$(L\otimes_K M)^Q=L\otimes_K M^Q,$$
this fixed field is purely inseparable over $L$, and $T^N/R$ is purely inseparable. The group actions need not be faithful. In particular, for finite extensions $k\subseteq e\subseteq F$ with compatible actions of finite groups $J\xrightarrow{\beta}G\xrightarrow{\alpha}H$, both arrows surjective, set $Q=\ker\beta$, $A=\ker\alpha$ and $N=\ker(\alpha\beta)$. If $F^Q/e$ and $e^A/k$ are purely inseparable, then $F^N/k$ is purely inseparable.

Purely inseparable means that every element has a $p$-power in the smaller field in characteristic $p>0$, and equality in characteristic zero. Field extensions, their finite degree and tensor products use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the algebra tensor product has multiplication $(l\otimes m)(l'\otimes m')=ll'\otimes mm'$.

proof.text: Put $E=M^Q$. Fixed elements form a subfield: automorphisms preserve $0,1,+,-,\cdot$ and send $x^{-1}$ to $g(x)^{-1}$. Since $Q$ fixes $L$, compatibility on $K$ implies that it fixes $K$, so $K\subseteq E$ and each $q\in Q$ acts $K$-linearly on $M$. The two factor maps to the field $T$ are injective: a unital map from a field has zero kernel, since a nonzero kernel element would give $1=0$ after multiplication by its inverse. We henceforth use these embeddings.

source.place: Agent argument from the field and fixed-element definitions; Definition Tag 09HE (definition-purely-inseparable) supplies the later convention.

proof.text: Choose a $K$-basis $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ of $L$ by applying the basis-extension statement to the empty independent set. Scalar extension gives an $M$-basis $(b_i\otimes1)$ of $L\otimes_K M$, and an $E$-basis with the same formula of $L\otimes_K E$. Thus the respective tensors have unique expressions $\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i$ and $\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$ with finitely supported coefficients. No finiteness of $L/K$ is required.

source.place: Section Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product); agent coordinate argument using the basis and scalar-extension statements.

proof.text: The tensor universal property gives $j:L\otimes_K E\to L\otimes_K M$, $l\otimes e\mapsto l\otimes e$; the multiplication formula in the statement makes it a ring map. In the bases of step 2 it sends $(e_i)$ to the same family in $M$, so it is injective. For $q\in Q$, the diagonal action on $z=\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i$ is $q(z)=\sum_i b_i\otimes q(m_i)$, since $q(b_i)=b_i$. Uniqueness of coordinates says that $z$ is fixed by every $q$ exactly when every $m_i\in E$. This is exactly the image of $j$, proving the asserted equality under $j$.

source.place: Section Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product); agent basis calculation, analogous to the invariant-coefficient calculation in Varieties Tag 038B.

proof.text: The image just identified is a field: if $0\ne z\in T^Q$, then $q(z^{-1})=q(z)^{-1}=z^{-1}$ for every $q$. Consequently $j$ identifies $L\otimes_K E$ with the fixed field $T^Q$, containing $L$ through $l\mapsto l\otimes1$.

In characteristic $p>0$, write any $z\in L\otimes_K E$ as a finite sum $\sum_{j=1}^r l_j\otimes e_j$, using generation by pure tensors and absorbing $K$-scalars into $l_j$. For each $e_j$, choose $n_j$ with $e_j^{p^{n_j}}\in K$, and choose $n\ge n_j$ for all $j$ (take $n=0$ for the empty sum). Then $e_j^{p^n}\in K$. The iterated Frobenius is a ring homomorphism, so $z^{p^n}=\sum_j l_j^{p^n}\otimes e_j^{p^n}=(\sum_j l_j^{p^n}e_j^{p^n})\otimes1\in L$. Thus $T^Q/L$ is purely inseparable. In characteristic zero $E=K$ by the hypothesis, and bilinearity gives $\sum_j l_j\otimes e_j=(\sum_j l_je_j)\otimes1$; hence $T^Q=L$.

source.place: Definition Tag 09HE (definition-purely-inseparable); the finite-sum calculation is the argument of Lemma Tag 09HH (lemma-purely-inseparable-elements); ring Frobenius as in Varieties Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius).

proof.text: Every element of $R\subseteq L^A$ is fixed by $N$, so $R\subseteq T^N$. Let $x\in T^N$. In characteristic $p>0$, step 5 gives $x^{p^n}=l\in L$. For every $g\in N$, equivariance of the embedding and preservation of powers give $g(l)=g(x)^{p^n}=x^{p^n}=l$. Thus $l\in L^{N/Q}=L^A$. By $L^A/R$ purely inseparable choose $m$ with $l^{p^m}\in R$; then $x^{p^{n+m}}\in R$. In characteristic zero step 5 puts $x$ in $L$, invariance puts it in $L^A$, and $L^A=R$. This proves $T^N/R$ purely inseparable.

source.place: Definition Tag 09HE (definition-purely-inseparable) and the explicit successive-power argument of Lemma Tag 09HG (lemma-purely-inseparable-permanence).

proof.text: For the final assertion, $Q\subseteq N$ and $\beta(N)=A$: if $a\in\ker\alpha$, choose $j\in J$ with $\beta(j)=a$; then $\alpha\beta(j)=1$, so $j\in N$. Compatibility of the field actions gives $k\subseteq F^N$. For $x\in F^N$ in characteristic $p>0$, the hypothesis $F^Q/e$ gives $x^{p^n}=y\in e$. For every $a\in A$, lift $a$ to $j\in N$ as above; then $a(y)=j(x^{p^n})=x^{p^n}=y$. Hence $y\in e^A$, and $e^A/k$ gives $y^{p^m}\in k$, so $x^{p^{n+m}}\in k$. In characteristic zero $F^Q=e$ and $e^A=k$; the same lift shows $F^N\subseteq e^A=k$. Together with the reverse inclusion this gives equality. No injectivity of any group action was used.
